$comment: THIS FILE IS THE WORKFLOW — edit it (plus terraform.tfvars) and you have your own multi-agent system. Both Terraform and CDK read it, so declaring a tool or agent here provisions its infrastructure; there are no IaC edits. BLOCKS: orchestrator (engine settings) · ui (branding) · guardrail (content safety) · authorization (who may approve/re-run/cancel/evaluate/delete) · tools (your data sources) · agents (one per folder under app/subagents/<id>/, except runtime "a2a" which has no folder) · steps (topology + review gates + branch conditions). EVERY AGENT reads the same way: name · kind · runtime · produces, then the model group (model · temperature · maxTokens) for a local agent OR the remote group (source|agentCard · skill · auth) for runtime "a2a", then what it may read (tool · corpus · access), then agentcore. EVERY TOOL reads: type · description, then where it lives, then how it is called, then filters, auth and policy. That order is not a convention you have to remember — `python3 format_workflow.py` rewrites the file into it, and `--check` fails CI if it drifts. WHICH KEYS ARE LEGAL WHERE is app/keys.json, and the allowed VALUES are app/vocabulary.json; both are framework-owned, and $schema above points your editor at the generated schema so it autocompletes keys, enumerates values and explains each one on hover. Prose reference: orchestrator/docs/WORKFLOW_REFERENCE.md

kb.description: Bedrock Knowledge Base over kb_docs/, on S3 Vectors, via a Gateway Lambda target. Each top-level folder under kb_docs/ is a corpus (doc_type) an agent can be scoped to.

websearch.description: AgentCore Web Search - a managed built-in Gateway connector. No API keys, no infrastructure, queries never leave AWS. us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1 only.

docs.description: AWS Knowledge MCP Server - managed by AWS, fronted by the Gateway over Streamable HTTP. Nothing to deploy, no credentials. Publishes five tools over live AWS content.

pricing.description: Real AWS on-demand unit prices, via an AWS Lambda target. The type="lambda" demonstration: a Lambda reaches what the Gateway cannot - a warehouse, an RDBMS, a VPC, or here a control-plane API with no MCP server in front of it. Returns RATES, never a total: a total needs usage volumes, which are a property of the workload and not of AWS.

toolSchema.name: aws_prices
toolSchema.description: On-demand unit prices for the named AWS services in one region, from the AWS Price List Query API. Unit rates only, never a total.

services.description: Comma-separated AWS service names, e.g. "Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda, DynamoDB".

region.description: Region code to price for, e.g. "us-east-1". Defaults to the deployment's own region.

lifecycle.description: Support and end-of-life dates for versioned products, via a REST API described by an OpenAPI schema. The type="openapi" demonstration: a service that already speaks HTTP and already has a contract needs no function and no MCP server - the Gateway loads the schema, publishes each operationId as a tool, and translates the call. Returns DATES as published, never a judgement about them.
